name: cart2pol
title: Coordinate Transformations
description: Cartesian coordinates to polar or cylindrical coordinates.
case: The point (1, 2, 3) as an angle, a radius, and a height.
args: A length-2 or length-3 vector, or a matrix with 2 or 3 columns.

name: cart2sph
title: Coordinate Transformations
description: Cartesian coordinates to spherical coordinates.
case: The point (1, 2, 3) as azimuth, elevation, and radius.
args: A length-3 vector, or a matrix with 3 columns.

name: pol2cart
title: Coordinate Transformations
description: Polar or cylindrical coordinates to Cartesian coordinates.
args: Angle, radius, and an optional height.

name: sph2cart
title: Coordinate Transformations
description: Spherical coordinates back to Cartesian coordinates.
case: Round trip of (1, 2, 3) through spherical coordinates.

name: complexstep
title: Complex Step Derivatives
description: First derivative from the imaginary part of a complex step.
args: Function that accepts a complex argument.
Point where the derivative is taken.
Complex step, required to be below 1e-15.

name: grad_csd
title: Complex Step Derivatives
description: Gradient of a scalar function by one complex step per coordinate.

name: hessian_csd
title: Complex Step Derivatives
description: Hessian from a complex step in one coordinate and Richardson in the other.

name: jacobian_csd
title: Complex Step Derivatives
description: Jacobian of a vector function by one complex step per column.

name: laplacian_csd
title: Complex Step Derivatives
description: Laplacian as the sum of pure second complex-step derivatives.

name: hessdiag
title: Hessian utilities
description: Diagonal of the Hessian, without the off-diagonal entries.

name: hessian
title: Hessian Matrix
description: Hessian from the three-point central difference, expanded to several variables.

name: hessvec
title: Hessian utilities
description: Product of the Hessian and a vector, without forming the full matrix.
args: Use a complex-step gradient when true.

name: laplacian
title: Laplacian Operator
description: Sum of the pure second central differences.

name: hurstexp
title: Hurst Exponent
description: Five Hurst estimates: simple, rescaled range, empirical, corrected empirical, and theoretical.
case: sin(1:64) with divisor bound 8 and the display turned off.
r: with(hurstexp(sin(1:64), d=8, display=FALSE), c(Hs, Hrs, He, Hal, Ht))
py: np.array([hurstexp(np.sin(np.arange(1, 65)), d=8, display=False)[k] for k in ('Hs', 'Hrs', 'He', 'Hal', 'Ht')])
args: Largest divisor used for the segments.
Print the five estimates when true.

name: fractalcurve
title: Fractal Curves
description: Coordinates of one of eight plane-filling curves.
case: Hilbert curve of order 2. The check is the x coordinates followed by the y coordinates.
args: One of the eight curve names.

name: haversine
title: Haversine Formula
description: Great-circle distance between two latitude-longitude locations.
args: Latitude and longitude, or a degrees-minutes-seconds string.

name: segm_distance
title: Segment Distance
description: Distance from a point to a segment, or between two segments.
case: Distance from (0.5, 1) to the segment from (0, 0) to (1, 0).
r: with(segm_distance(c(0, 0), c(1, 0), c(0.5, 1)), c(d, p, q))
args: A point, or one endpoint of a second segment.
The other endpoint. Empty means p3 is a point.

name: segm_intersect
title: Segment Intersection
description: Whether two closed segments in the plane cross.
case: The diagonals of the unit square.
args: 2 by 2 matrix, one endpoint per row.

name: inpolygon
title: Polygon Region
description: 1 where a point lies inside a polygon, 0 outside. The result has the shape of x.
usage: inpolygon(x, y, xp, yp, boundary = FALSE)
case: Three query points against the unit square.
args: Count the boundary as inside when true.

name: rectint
title: Rectangle Intersection Areas
description: Area of the overlap of two axis-aligned rectangles.
args: Left, bottom, width, and height, or a matrix of those rows.

name: arclength
title: Arc Length of a Curve
description: Romberg estimate of the length of a parametric curve.
case: Quarter unit circle, at most 8 Romberg rows.
r: with(arclength(function(t) c(cos(t), sin(t)), 0, pi/2, nmax=8), c(length, niter, rel.err))
py: np.array([arclength(lambda t: np.concatenate([np.cos(np.atleast_1d(t)), np.sin(np.atleast_1d(t))]), 0, np.pi/2, nmax=8)[k] for k in ('length', 'niter', 'rel.err')])
args: Parametric map. A vector of t returns the coordinates concatenated.

name: kriging
title: Interpolation by Kriging
description: Ordinary or simple kriging at new sites.
case: Ordinary kriging of four corner values at the center.
args: Sites where a value is requested.

name: affineproj
title: Linear Projection onto a Subspace
description: Projection onto the affine set C x = b. The distance is the norm of the projection.
usage: affineproj(x0, C, b, unbound = TRUE, maxniter = 100)
case: Project (0, 5) onto the line whose first coordinate is 2.
args: Ignore the positivity constraint when true.
Iteration cap for the positive case.

name: linearproj
title: Linear Projection onto a Subspace
description: Projection of the columns of B onto the column space of A.
py: (lambda z: np.concatenate([np.ravel(z['P'], order='F'), np.ravel(z['Q'], order='F')]))(linearproj(np.eye(2), np.array([[3.], [4.]])))
args: Points to project, one column each.

name: kabsch
title: Solving the Procrustes Problem
description: Weighted rotation and translation that align two point sets.
case: Align a 2 by 3 point set with equal weights.
r: local({A<-matrix(1:6, 2, 3); B<-matrix(c(2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5), 2, 3); with(kabsch(A, B), c(U, R, d))})
py: (lambda z: np.concatenate([np.ravel(z['U'], order='F'), np.ravel(z['R'], order='F'), np.ravel(z['d'])]))(kabsch(np.array([1,2,3,4,5,6], dtype=float).reshape((2, 3), order='F'), np.array([2,1,4,3,6,5], dtype=float).reshape((2, 3), order='F')))
args: Points to align, same size as A.
Column weights. Equal weights when omitted.

name: procrustes
title: Solving the Procrustes Problem
description: Orthogonal matrix that rotates B toward A, and the residual distance.
case: Orthogonal alignment of two 2 by 3 matrices.
r: local({A<-matrix(1:6, 2, 3); B<-matrix(c(2, 1, 4, 3, 6, 5), 2, 3); with(procrustes(A, B), c(P, Q, d))})
py: (lambda z: np.concatenate([np.ravel(z['P'], order='F'), np.ravel(z['Q'], order='F'), [z['d']]]))(procrustes(np.array([1,2,3,4,5,6], dtype=float).reshape((2, 3), order='F'), np.array([2,1,4,3,6,5], dtype=float).reshape((2, 3), order='F')))
args: Matrix to rotate. Same size as A.

name: trigApprox
title: Trigonometric Approximation
description: Evaluate the trigonometric polynomial fitted to equally spaced samples.
case: Degree-1 fit of (1, 2, 1, 0), evaluated at 0 and 1.
args: Abscissae where the polynomial is evaluated.

name: trigPoly
title: Trigonometric Polynomial
description: Cosine and sine coefficients of equally spaced samples.

name: approx_entropy
title: Approximate and Sample Entropy
description: Approximate entropy of a series at a given embedding dimension.
args: Tolerance. The default is 0.2 times the sample deviation.

name: sample_entropy
title: Approximate and Sample Entropy
description: Sample entropy of a series.

name: findpeaks
title: Find Peaks
description: Peaks as rows of value, index, left index, and right index. Indices stay 1-based.
usage: findpeaks(x, nups = 1, ndowns = nups, zero = '0', peakpat = NULL, minpeakheight = -Inf, minpeakdistance = 1, threshold = 0, npeaks = 0, sortstr = FALSE)
args: Rising samples required before a peak.
Falling samples required after a peak.
Character used for a flat step.
Maximum number of peaks. 0 keeps them all.

name: findmins
title: Find All Minima
description: Local minima on a grid of subintervals, each refined by Brent.

name: findzeros
title: Find All Roots
description: Roots on a grid of subintervals, each refined by Brent.
case: Root of x - 0.3 on [-1, 1], using 10 subintervals.
args: Tolerance for the sign change and the bracket minimizer.

name: findintervals
title: Find Interval Indices
description: 1-based indices of the interval endpoints that contain x.

name: gradient
title: Discrete Gradient (Matlab Style)
description: Central differences of a vector or a matrix.

name: grad
title: Numerical Gradient
description: Central-difference gradient of a scalar function.
args: Point where the gradient is taken.

name: jacobian
title: Numerical Gradient
description: Central-difference Jacobian of a vector function.
args: Point where the Jacobian is taken.

name: fderiv
title: Numerical Differentiation
description: Derivative of a stated order by a finite-difference stencil.
usage: fderiv(f, x, n = 1, h = 0, method = c('central', 'forward', 'backward'), ...)
args: Step. 0 selects a step from the order.

name: numderiv
title: Richardson's Numerical Derivative
description: First derivative by Richardson extrapolation.
py: np.array([numderiv(lambda x: x**2, 2)[k] for k in ('df', 'rel.err', 'niter')])
args: Stop when the relative change drops below this.

name: numdiff
title: Richardson's Numerical Derivative
description: Richardson derivative at each entry of a vector.
case: Derivative of x^2 at 1 and at 2.
args: Passed through. Each inner call uses machine epsilon.

name: fornberg
title: Fornberg's Finite Difference Approximation
description: Derivative of tabulated data at requested abscissae.
case: First derivative of the squares of 1:5, at 2 and 3.
args: Abscissae where the derivative is requested.

name: movavg
title: Moving Average Filters
description: Simple, triangular, weighted, modified, exponential, or recursive moving average.
case: Simple moving average of 1:10 with window 3.
args: s, t, w, m, e, or r.

name: detrend
title: Remove Linear Trends
description: Subtract a constant or a continuous piecewise-linear trend.
args: Vector or matrix. A vector is treated as one column.
constant or linear. A unique prefix is enough.

name: hampel
title: Hampel Filter
description: Replace an isolated outlier by the window median. Indices stay 1-based.
args: How many scaled deviations count as an outlier.

name: cutpoints
title: Find Cutting Points
description: The widest gaps in a sorted sample, above a quantile of the gap sizes.
args: Maximum number of gaps to return.

name: piecewise
title: Piecewise Linear Function
description: Signed area under a polyline, and the abscissae where it crosses zero.
args: Use absolute area when true. The argument name is abs.

name: whittaker
title: Whittaker Smoothing
description: Smooth a series by penalizing squared differences. The penalty argument is lambda_ in Python.
args: Penalty weight. Call it positionally or as lambda_ in Python.

name: geo_median
title: Geometric Median
description: Weiszfeld geometric median, started one step away from the coordinate means.
case: Four corners of the unit square.
r: with(geo_median(matrix(c(0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1), 4, 2, byrow=TRUE)), c(p, d, reltol, niter))
args: Stop when the step falls below this.

name: circlefit
title: Fitting a Circle
description: Center and radius of the circle fitted to planar points. The RMS error is printed.
case: Five points on the unit circle.

name: stereographic
title: Stereographic Projection
description: Stereographic projection from the last coordinate.
args: Points as columns. The last row is the pole coordinate.

name: stereographic_inv
title: Stereographic Projection
description: Inverse stereographic projection.

name: cross
title: Vector Cross Product
description: Cross product of two length-3 vectors, or of matrices with 3 columns or 3 rows.
args: Length-3 vector, or a matrix with 3 columns or 3 rows.

name: crossn
title: n-dimensional Vector Cross Product
description: The vector orthogonal to n vectors in dimension n + 1.
args: A length-2 vector, or an n by (n + 1) matrix.

name: odregress
title: Orthogonal Distance Regression
description: Hyperplane fitted by orthogonal distance.
case: Four points near the line y = x.
r: with(odregress(c(1, 2, 3, 4), c(1.1, 1.9, 3.2, 3.8)), c(coeff, ssq, err, fitted, resid, normal))
args: Predictors, a vector or a matrix.

name: L1linreg
title: L1 Linear Regression
description: Iteratively reweighted least squares for an L1 fit.

name: curvefit
title: Parametric Curve Fit
description: Polynomial fit of a parametric curve, optionally through prescribed points.
usage: curvefit(u, x, y, n, U = NULL, V = NULL)
case: Degree 2 fit of (u^2, 2u + 1) on six knots from 0 to 1.
r: local({u<-seq(0, 1, length.out=6); with(curvefit(u, u^2, 2*u+1, 2), c(xp, yp, px, py))})
py: (lambda u, z: np.concatenate([z['xp'], z['yp'], np.ravel(z['px'], order='F'), np.ravel(z['py'], order='F')]))(np.linspace(0, 1, 6), curvefit(np.linspace(0, 1, 6), np.linspace(0, 1, 6)**2, 2*np.linspace(0, 1, 6)+1, 2))

name: poisson2disk
title: Poisson Disk Sampling
description: Random points in a rectangle with a minimum separation. The check is a predicate, not the points.
usage: poisson2disk(n, a = 1, b = 1, m = 10, info = TRUE)
case: Eight points in the unit square. The check is the row count, two columns, and that every coordinate lies in (0, 1).
done: The points differ between languages. Both predicates are 8, 2, and 1.
r: local({p <- poisson2disk(8, a=1, b=1, m=6, info=FALSE); c(nrow(p), ncol(p), as.numeric(all(p[,1] > 0 & p[,1] < 1 & p[,2] > 0 & p[,2] < 1)))})
py: (lambda p: np.array([p.shape[0], p.shape[1], float(np.all((p[:,0] > 0) & (p[:,0] < 1) & (p[:,1] > 0) & (p[:,1] < 1)))]))(poisson2disk(8, a=1, b=1, m=6, info=False))
args: Candidates tried around each accepted point.

name: golden_ratio
title: Golden Ratio Search
description: Golden-section search for a minimum on a bounded interval.
args: Stop when the bracket is narrower than this.

name: combs
title: Generate Combinations
description: Combinations of the values themselves, in lexicographic order.

name: randcomb
title: Random Combination
description: A random combination without replacement. The check is a predicate, not the draw.
case: Four values drawn from 1:10. The check is the length and that every value belongs to 1:10.
done: The draw differs between languages. Both predicates are 4 and 1.

name: sumalt
title: Alternating Series Acceleration
description: Cohen-Villegas-Zagier acceleration of an alternating series.
args: Term as a function of k, starting at 0.

name: runge
title: Runge Function
description: The Runge function 1 / (1 + 25 x^2).

name: aitken
title: Aitken' Method
description: Aitken acceleration of the fixed-point iteration x = f(x).
case: cos started at 0.5. The iteration hits the default cap.
args: Stop when successive values agree to this tolerance.

name: agmean
title: Arithmetic-geometric Mean
description: Arithmetic-geometric mean of two numbers.

name: invlap
title: Inverse Laplacian
description: Numerical inverse Laplace transform on a time interval.
usage: invlap(Fs, t1, t2, nnt, a = 6, ns = 20, nd = 19)
case: Inverse of 1/(s + 1) from 0.2 to 1.5 on 8 nodes.

name: lebesgue
title: Lebesgue Constant
description: Maximum of the Lebesgue function for interpolation nodes.

name: rmserr
title: Accuracy Measures
description: Mean absolute, squared, root squared, percentage, normalized, and relative errors.
r: with(rmserr(1:5, c(1.1, 2, 2.9, 4.2, 5)), c(mae, mse, rmse, mape, nmse, rstd))
args: Print the six measures when true.

name: lsqsep
title: Nonlinear Least-Squares Fitting
description: Separable nonlinear least squares. The nonlinear parameters go through Levenberg-Marquardt.
usage: lsqsep(flist, p0, xdata, ydata, const = TRUE)
case: One exponential plus a constant, started at -0.4, on 12 points of 1 + 2 exp(-0.5 x).
r: local({x<-seq(0, 2, length.out=12); y<-1+2*exp(-0.5*x); with(lsqsep(list(function(b, x) exp(b*x)), -0.4, x, y), c(a0, a, b, ssq))})
py: (lambda xx, yy, z: np.concatenate([[z['a0']], np.ravel(z['a']), np.ravel(z['b']), [z['ssq']]]))(np.linspace(0, 2, 12), 1+2*np.exp(-0.5*np.linspace(0, 2, 12)), lsqsep([lambda b, x: np.exp(np.asarray(b, dtype=float)*np.asarray(x, dtype=float))], -0.4, np.linspace(0, 2, 12), 1+2*np.exp(-0.5*np.linspace(0, 2, 12))))
args: Include a constant column when true.

name: mexpfit
title: Multi-exponential Fitting
description: Sum of exponentials fitted by separable least squares.
usage: mexpfit(x, y, p0, w = NULL, const = TRUE, options = list())
case: 1 + 2 exp(-0.5 x) on 12 points from 0 to 2, started at -0.4.
r: local({x<-seq(0, 2, length.out=12); y<-1+2*exp(-0.5*x); with(mexpfit(x, y, p0=-0.4), c(a0, a, b, ssq))})
args: Starting rates. Duplicates are dropped. Zero is rejected.
Include a constant term when true.
tau, tolx, tolg, and maxeval. Unspecified keys keep the mexpfit defaults.

name: rat
title: Continuous Fractions (Matlab Style)
description: Continued-fraction text. The closing bracket is written only when there are at least three terms.

name: rats
title: Continuous Fractions (Matlab Style)
description: Prints each ratio and returns the numeric value. The printed line is the check.
case: The printed ratio for pi, without the space cat inserts before the newline.
py: (lambda s: (lambda cm: (cm.__enter__(), rats(np.pi), cm.__exit__(None, None, None), s.getvalue().strip())[-1])(__import__('contextlib').redirect_stdout(s)))(__import__('io').StringIO())

name: newtonsys
title: Newton Method for Nonlinear Systems
description: Newton iteration for a nonlinear system, with a numerical Jacobian by default.
usage: newtonsys(Ffun, x0, Jfun = NULL, ..., maxiter = 100, tol = .Machine$double.eps^0.5)
r: with(newtonsys(function(z) c(z[1]^2 - 1, z[2] - 2), c(0.5, 1)), c(zero, fnorm, niter))
py: (lambda z: np.concatenate([z['zero'], [z['fnorm'], z['niter']]]))(newtonsys(lambda z: np.array([z[0]**2 - 1, z[1] - 2]), [0.5, 1]))
args: Jacobian. The numerical Jacobian is used when omitted.
Stop when the step or the residual is small.
